items.title: Staged attach onto a dirty target: overlap, backup, trial merge, rules, exact land
items.action: Copy the planned files first: docs/plans/1018/tests/tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_dirty.py, test_attach_worktree_config_source.py, test_attach_worktree_index.py and test_attach_worktree_script.py to tests/skills/ (the last two replace the current files; the script file only drops three tests whose behavior changes). Spec items 2-6, 8 and 9 for staged mode (D3 split): a) attach_worktree.py inserts Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / 'lib' on sys.path (as d-w/commands/new_worktree.py:36 does), imports its sibling attach_merge by plain import, and calls activate(load_config(root)) once (D2), root being project_root(target) when that checkout holds .claude/harness.json and main_worktree(target) (harness_lib.project) otherwise, so a target branch checked out in a linked worktree still gets an untracked harness.json from the main checkout. b) check_git_version(version_output: str) -> None raises AttachError naming git 2.40 below 2.40; attach() calls it on `git --version` before any other step. c) Rules: AutoResolve from harness_lib.config; repeatable --auto-resolve PATTERN=SIDE (argparse append; a value without '=' or a side other than worktree/branch is a usage error); rules = config rules then flag rules; matching with fnmatch.fnmatchcase (D6); a path two rules give different sides raises AttachError naming the path and the word ambiguous. d) Snapshot: target_head and the dirty set from `status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=no` (both sides of a rename, staged and unstaged). e) Worktree commit: the scratch index (scratch_index, add -A), write-tree, commit-tree -p HEAD, never touching the worktree's index or refs; changed paths = diff --name-only --no-renames from patch_base() to that commit. f) Overlap: changed paths in the dirty set that no rule covers refuse, naming them (a rule of either side lifts a staged overlap: spec item 6 over item 3's text, DesignEvolution P2); a path the move adds that is untracked in the target refuses, naming it with the word untracked. g) Backup: taken in the land (i), right after the race check, never before the trial, so the sha a report prints always holds the dirty state that land overwrites (DesignEvolution P3). h) Trial: merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<patch_base> <target_head> <worktree commit> (--name-only -z --no-messages, parsed per git-merge-tree(1)). Ruled conflicted paths take the chosen side's blob or deletion into the result tree through a temporary index (read-tree, update-index --cacheinfo / --force-remove, write-tree). Unruled conflicts left: refuse naming the paths and saying to commit the worktree's changes in the worktree first when the worktree is dirty; until TASK-3 lands, the clean-worktree case refuses the same way without the commit advice. i) Land: re-read target HEAD and dirty set (a change refuses: rerun); then the backup, `git stash create` in the target (empty output = clean target, reported as such); then `git apply --index` of `diff --binary --full-index <target_head> <final tree>` excluding every rule-governed dirty path (:(exclude,literal) pathspecs). Only after it succeeds, each worktree-ruled dirty path gets the final tree's blob written and staged (or is removed and unstaged when the final tree lacks it); a branch-ruled dirty path is left as it is. j) Report: staged N file(s) on <branch>, nothing committed; a line holding the word backup and the stash sha (or saying the target was clean); each overwritten dirty path; undo lines `git -C <target> restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <paths>` for the clean paths and, per overwritten path, `restore --source=<backup>^2 --staged -- <path>` then `restore --source=<backup> --worktree -- <path>`; `next: git diff --cached`. A path is quoted only when it holds whitespace. k) Remove tracked_changes, unmerged, conflict_message and the apply --3way path; the dirty-target refusal at attach() stays for --committed only until TASK-3. Every refusal changes nothing in the target. Functions under 50 lines; no first or second person in comments.

items.title: Resolution in the worktree: rebase loop, exit 2, --continue/--abort, --committed rebase
items.action: Copy docs/plans/1018/tests/tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_resolve.py and test_attach_worktree_continue_backup.py to tests/skills/ first. Spec items 5 (committed routing), 6 (committed overlap), 7, 8 and the Interface: a) attach_resolve.py owns the state file `git rev-parse --git-path harness-attach.json` resolved in the worktree: JSON with target_branch, target_checkout, mode (staged|committed), target_head, original_head, patch_base, rules. Written before the rebase starts; removed once the land succeeds or --abort runs. A plain run while it exists refuses naming --continue and --abort. b) Resolution needs a clean worktree (status --porcelain, untracked included): otherwise refuse, naming the conflicted paths and saying to commit in the worktree first. Staged mode builds one squash commit (commit-tree HEAD^{tree} -p <patch_base>) and runs `rebase --onto <target_head> <patch_base> <squash>`; --committed runs `rebase --onto <target_head> <patch_base>` with no squash. Every rebase step runs with GIT_EDITOR=true. c) At each stop: conflicted paths from `diff --name-only --diff-filter=U -z`; a ruled path takes stage 3 (the replayed worktree commit) for worktree or stage 2 (the target side) for branch, a side without the path becoming git rm; then git add. An ambiguous rule mid-rebase aborts the rebase, resets to original_head, removes the state and refuses. Nothing unruled left: rebase --continue and loop. Otherwise write the state, print the paths, the worktree path and the --continue / --abort commands to stdout, exit 2 (a StopForResolution exception main() maps to 2). d) --continue and --abort (mutually exclusive) read the state and take no TARGET; a TARGET, --committed or --auto-resolve that differs from the state refuses and keeps the state. --continue with a rebase in progress: unmerged paths left stop again with exit 2; else continue the loop, then race check and land (TASK-2 land for staged, the final tree being HEAD^{tree}; merge --ff-only for --committed). Every land path (the first run, --continue with or without a rebase in progress, the D4 restart) runs `git stash create` in the target right after its race check and before the apply or merge, and prints that sha in the report and the undo lines; the state file holds no backup, so no report reuses a sha an earlier run took. A race refusal keeps the state and the resolved commits and names --continue. --continue with no rebase in progress (D4): patch_base := the state's target_head, then rerun the flow from the snapshot against the current target HEAD (another stop is possible), updating the state. --abort: rebase --abort when in progress, reset --hard to original_head (exact: the worktree was clean), remove the state, report the worktree's HEAD, exit 0 (D5). e) --committed: drop both refusals (target moved, cut not in the target); keep the uncommitted and no-commits refusals. A dirty overlap always refuses, rules or not. When target_head is the merge base and the cut (if any) is in target_head, fast-forward as today; otherwise run the trial first (ambiguity refuses before the worktree is touched), then the rebase. Land: race check, then the backup (`git stash create`), then merge --ff-only; report the commit count, the backup and `undo: git -C <target> reset --keep <target_head>`. f) Rewrite the module docstring: the interface line with --auto-resolve, --continue and --abort, exit codes 0/1/2, the dirty-target rule, no conflict markers in the target. Functions under 50 lines.

items.title: Rules exception and the a-w, d-w and README texts
items.action: Copy docs/plans/1018/tests/tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_docs.py to tests/skills/ first. a) HARNESS_RULES.md:25-26: append to the history-rewrite rule the one exception: attach_worktree.py (harness:a-w) rebases and squashes the worktree's own unpushed commits inside a d-w worktree during an attach; the agent resolves conflicts there and reruns the script with --continue or --abort, never running rebase, merge or cherry-pick itself. b) a-w SKILL.md: argument-hint gains [--auto-resolve PATTERN=SIDE ...] [--continue | --abort]; the opening paragraph and mode table describe the trial merge and the --committed rebase onto a moved target; the clean-target bullet becomes the overlap rule (dirty paths the move does not write stay; an overlap or an untracked collision refuses; the backup sha and the path-scoped undo); the conflict bullets become the resolution loop (exit 2, edit and git add in the worktree, --continue; --abort on any ambiguity, then report); --auto-resolve and the attach.auto_resolve key, with the ambiguous refusal; the rules exception; --committed still only on the developer's explicit ask. No reset --hard and no 'no tracked changes' remain. c) d-w SKILL.md:65-69: the finishing bullet drops the three-way-conflict case and says a-w may stop with exit 2 for resolution in the worktree, where a-w runs the rebase and the agent reruns with --continue or --abort. d) README.md:32: the a-w row states the overlap rule, the trial merge, the resolution loop (--continue / --abort) and the --committed rebase; no 'no tracked changes', no 'leaves markers'.

decisions.question: Where does the AutoResolve dataclass live?

options.summary: harness_lib.config, beside the attach.auto_resolve key that builds it
the a-w commands folder, with the config holding plain dicts

decisions.rationale: One frozen type serves the config load and the driver; the config stays typed and hashable like CannedSet.

decisions.question: Which checkout's .claude/harness.json supplies attach.auto_resolve?

options.summary: load_config(project_root(target checkout)) when that checkout holds .claude/harness.json, else load_config(main_worktree(target checkout))

decisions.rationale: The rules govern what lands on the target branch, and the target checkout is the project the developer configures; an untracked harness.json never reaches a worktree. A target branch checked out in a linked worktree (a collector) lacks that untracked file too, so the main checkout supplies it there; a tracked harness.json is present in every checkout, so the target's own copy wins. test_untracked_main_checkout_rules_apply_to_a_target_in_a_linked_worktree pins it.

decisions.question: How does attach_worktree.py split as it grows?

options.summary: attach_worktree.py (CLI, preconditions, flow, removal), attach_merge.py (snapshot, overlap, backup, trial merge, rules, land), attach_resolve.py (state file, rebase loop, --continue, --abort)

decisions.rationale: The spec leaves the split to the builder and allows it by concern; three concerns, each under the 50-line function rule, keep each file readable.

decisions.question: What does --continue do when no rebase is in progress (after a race refusal)?

options.summary: rerun the flow from the snapshot (spec item 2) with patch_base set to the target_head the finished rebase went onto, and land against the current target HEAD
re-snapshot and land the diff from the new target HEAD to the resolved tree

decisions.rationale: A diff from the new target HEAD to a tree built on the old one reverts the late target commit; measuring from the old target_head carries only the worktree's work. DesignEvolution entry records it.

decisions.question: What exit code does a successful --abort return?
decisions.rationale: The abort did what was asked; 1 stays the refusal code and 2 the resolution stop.

decisions.question: How do rule patterns match paths?

options.summary: fnmatch.fnmatchcase over the repo-relative POSIX path

decisions.rationale: The same rule set must land the same files on every OS; case folding on Windows would widen a rule there only.
